punchline: James Allen ends his book on the power of thought with a shopkeeper: customers always prefer the one who stays calm.
thirty_sec: James Allen closes As a Man Thinketh with a chapter called Serenity. Calmness of mind, he says, is one of the jewels of wisdom, and it comes from long effort at self-control. His example is an ordinary trader whose business grows as he gets steadier, because people prefer dealing with someone even-tempered. He compares the calm person to a shade tree in a thirsty land, and ends: keep your hand on the helm of thought.
